scope: Existing E08 genuine-entry integration clauses; separate from the 52 metadata literal outcomes.
genuine_object_rule: K_A and K_B mean actual separately executed future kernel namespaces; A means the actual Core returned or retained by K_A entry. Bindings, reports, snapshots and refs must come from those actual implementations. No object.__new__, object.__setattr__, decoded dictionary, serialized ready flag or imitation type may manufacture a binding/Core/report/lease to reach a guard.

scenarios.setup: Genuine K_A services with one immutable valid binding, independent envelope and matching actual EntryPlan; original provider starts at 100.
scenarios.action: Observe actual entry through policy validation and the first subsequent output/original/helper operation.
expected: The original first sample and sole Origin/Core/Registry/raw-store/facades exist before bounded policy capture or graph work.
Policy attempted/error/prepared/issued observations belong to that same Core; no helper import is needed to validate policy.
No reserve-output callback, original-file open, compiler/helper execution or continuation occurs before timely EXECUTION policy issuance.
The start 100, work end 395, hard end 400 and original provider identity remain unchanged.

scenarios.setup: Genuine AUTHORING binding/envelope containing the frozen planned/unbuilt literal data; final binary hashes remain null with reasons.
scenarios.action: Enter, observe the cached AUTHORING_ONLY report, then attempt each ordinary output-reservation, original7, captured-compiler and continuation surface.
expected: The same Core may return an immutable AUTHORING_ONLY data report without constructing fictitious executable FileSpecs or final output hashes.
All output/original/compiler/continuation attempts refuse before dispatch; all corresponding callback counts remain zero.
Readonly snapshot/report observation remains possible and does not imply runtime admission.

scenarios.setup: Genuine EXECUTION binding/envelope and independently frozen actual helper source pins/FileSpecs in the ordered basis; the selected future implementation supplies the concrete helper prefix.
scenarios.action: Validate, reserve the original output namespace, capture/load actual selected helpers, and attach their non-owning adapters.
expected: The timely public report is the same object retained as prepared, and actual policy eligibility remains Core-owned.
One Core, Origin, nonce, Registry, raw store, port/sink/journal facades and original clock provider survive the complete prefix and helper handoff by is identity.
Helper execution uses captured authenticated bytes and the actual K_A namespace; it does not create a replacement owner or rely on an old Source3/Source4 constructor.
Policy acceptance supplements existing FileSpec, captured-DAG, quotas, output ownership, live identity/hash and lease checks; it does not replace them.

scenarios.setup: Actual immutable K_A binding construction plus its caller-owned input lists; for the foreign branch construct a genuine equal-valued binding from separately executed K_B.
scenarios.action: Mutate original containers after construction/capture; try ordinary field/service/class selection rebinding; or supply the genuine K_B binding to K_A entry.
expected: Detached immutable binding/envelope/report values do not alias mutable caller containers.
Ordinary rebinding refuses or cannot alter the already selected Core binding/class reference; no replacement callable/class is followed.
A same-name/equal-source/equal-value foreign binding is refused through the genuine namespace/type boundary before policy/output/original progress.
The original state, start sample, prior observations and first error remain retained; no numeric-start adoption or alternate binding/check/clock argument is accepted.

scenarios.setup: Actual policy success or first refusal is already retained in a genuine Core.
scenarios.action: Call validate_external_policy again; repeatedly read public report, detached report data and actual cached snapshots; offer corrected/favorable metadata after a failed attempt.
expected: Validation remains once-only, including after an earlier refusal or incomplete attempt; a second attempt cannot replace the binding/report or retry graph work.
Cold getters/snapshots do not call the provider, validator, report constructor, output backend or original-file backend.
No corrected metadata or favorable clock heals failure, creates eligibility or renews the original budget; the retained first error remains the original object.

scenarios.setup: Actual valid metadata on the genuine Core; a controlled original MemoryError occurs before the actual immutable report constructor returns.
scenarios.action: Run policy issuance through that real allocation boundary and inspect retained diagnostics/snapshot data after unwind.
expected: The same original MemoryError and original clock/Core remain retained.
Prepared report, public issued report and execution eligibility remain absent/false because no report return was observed.
There is no output/original/compiler/continuation dispatch, retry, fabricated report or replacement state.

scenarios.setup: The actual immutable report constructor has returned a valid 12-field report; the final original work-clock check reaches 395 or an original allocation/bookkeeping error interrupts subsequent issuance.
scenarios.action: Observe actual retained prepared versus issued policy state and the genuine diagnostic token resolver after unwind.
expected: The original returned report object is retained as prepared before the throwable final eligibility step; its values are inspectable in immutable snapshot data.
Public manifest_policy_report remains None and actual execution eligibility remains false; no successful status in prepared data opens a gate.
The original clock/deadline or original allocation exception is preserved, with no output/original/compiler dispatch or retry.
Cold reads preserve the same prepared data and do not heal, resample or republish it.

scenarios.setup: Actual detached report data, or an ordinary dictionary carrying EXECUTION_BASIS_VALIDATED, exists without an issued same-Core eligibility fact.
scenarios.action: Use only ordinary public surfaces to try treating the data/status/digests as a binding, state view, continuation, native lease, child binding or execution gate.
expected: No parsed report, hash, approved/ready flag or successful status creates an Origin/nonce/Core/ref/continuation/lease/child/image authority or actual file admission.
The report retains exactly its 12 declared data keys; provenance/control authority remains the genuine live Core.
Unsupported native/physical routes remain unavailable; no fake typed object is constructed to simulate a positive authority branch.

scenarios.setup: A genuine timely EXECUTION report is issued; later original work retains a known committed usable handle and an unrelated original failure in the same Core.
scenarios.action: Attempt a different fresh known-right CloseHandle below the original hard end, then the separate branch at hard end 400.
expected: An already valid policy gate does not become a blanket primary-is-None check; a fresh nonstopped cleanup call below the original hard end retains its legal once-only opportunity.
Stopped same-call caches remain quarantined and committed raw facts stay known; cleanup does not heal/retry failed work or replace the original error.
At the original hard boundary all dispatch remains blocked, with known rights honestly unclosed/unknown and no renewed timer or policy validation.

scenarios.setup: Use only the genuine public immutable-binding constructor: either a wrong exact list/pin shape or an otherwise valid bounded shell containing a semantic/domain fault from the frozen literals.
scenarios.action: Attempt ordinary construction and, only if an actual binding returns, the genuine entry call.
expected: Constructor-only wrong shape/container/custom-leaf refusals occur before entry; no original-clock/Core facts are claimed for them.
All 52 current literal bindings satisfy the constructor shell, so their semantic/domain/graph refusals occur after original sample/Core policy entry as predeclared.
No object.__new__, object.__setattr__, counterfeit holder or decoded data is used to force unreachable binding states through Core.

limitations: These are declarative future integration scenarios, not another set of executed tests or metadata literal outcomes.
Concrete future source/helper pins and actual fault seams must be frozen under a later implementation/test scope.
External configuration remains an explicit TCB assumption, not launcher authentication, live resource admission or a physical/native capability.
Historical E16 actions, native25, full real roster/new84, resource fit, science and human gates remain unqualified.
